skill.description: Create local interactive reports from authorized personal finance records. Explore spending, income, transfers, cash movement, and optional daily allowances in English or Simplified Chinese.
skill.summary: Visualize reconciled personal finances with local charts, transaction details, period comparisons, and optional daily allowances.

No evidence found of prompt injection, credential collection, unauthorized financial actions, or transaction exfiltration.

content.user_title: Visualize Personal Finances in a Local Report
content.value_statement: Financial records can obscure spending patterns when transfers, refunds, and shared purchases are mixed together. This skill reconciles authorized records and creates local interactive charts with transaction details and optional daily allowances.
actual_capabilities: Render normalized JSON or CSV as interactive spending, income, transfer, and cash movement views.
Compare day, week, month, and year periods with chart drill-down and searchable transaction tables.
Apply confirmed personal shares, exact full-refund mappings, transfer settlements, and pending purchase treatment.
Calculate daily allowances with monthly resets, daily caps, coverage checks, and historical or manual category shares.
Display reports in English or Simplified Chinese with theme switching and reorderable cards.
Serve reports from memory over a tokenized loopback URL or create an explicitly requested private HTML export.
limitations: Raw bank exports need explicit field mapping; PDF extraction depends on authorized tools available to the agent.
Each report supports one currency with two decimal places and performs no currency conversion.
Input is limited to 25 MiB, 100,000 transactions, and 50 years of coverage.
Persistent budget synchronization requires a separately provided authenticated same-origin backend; the bundled server does not implement it.

use_cases.title: Review Household Spending
use_cases.description: Separate household purchases, internal transfers, and confirmed shared costs to compare monthly personal spending.

use_cases.title: Distinguish Income From Transfers
use_cases.description: Review supplied personal records and distinguish confirmed freelance income from reimbursements, loans, and unexplained deposits.

use_cases.title: Track a Daily Allowance
use_cases.description: Use confirmed spending and current month coverage to review a daily allowance and category reference shares.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a Fictional Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Show a clearly labeled fictional finance demo in English. Use the bundled local report and do not read my files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: explore the report without personal data.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Normalized Export
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [authorized CSV path] for [coverage period] in [currency]. Confirm date and sign mappings, ask about unresolved transactions, then show a local report.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: analyze an authorized transaction export.

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile Multiple Statements
prompt_templates.prompt: Reconcile [authorized statements] for [period] in [currency]. Ask about uncertain duplicates, account ownership, personal shares, refunds, and repayments before final charts.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a Daily Allowance
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [authorized records], prepare a daily allowance with [daily cap], [timezone], and [included expense groups]. Confirm classifications and coverage first. Use historical category shares when available; keep changes in page memory.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: configure budgeting without a remote integration.

output_examples.input: Fictional complete January records show USD 3,000 income and USD 1,200 expenses, with no refunds, transfers, or pending transactions.
output: External cash movement: USD 3,000.00 inflow, USD 1,200.00 outflow, and USD 1,800.00 net increase.
Charts provide transaction drill-down for the supplied coverage.

output_examples.input: Fictional records contain a USD 100 February purchase and its confirmed full USD 100 March refund.
output: The confirmed full-refund mapping removes the purchase from February personal spending.
Cash movement retains the February outflow and March inflow on their original dates.

output_examples.input: Fictional June 21 budget: USD 30 daily cap, complete coverage, USD 600 spent before today, and USD 12 spent today.
output: Opening allowance: USD 30.00 across 10 remaining days, including today.
Remaining monthly budget after today's spending: USD 288.00.

best_practices: Confirm coverage, currency, amount signs, and uncertain transaction relationships before finalizing charts.
Use account aliases and standard input for newly normalized records; keep exports and report URLs private.
Check displayed totals and transaction details against source evidence, and use fictional data for saved screenshots.
anti_patterns: Do not classify unknown deposits as income or match refunds and repayments using similar amounts alone.
Do not publish reports or place real transaction data in repositories, examples, screenshots, or public issues.
Do not present incomplete coverage, unresolved classifications, or stale daily allowances as a complete financial picture.

faq.question: Which inputs can I use?
faq.answer: The renderer accepts normalized JSON and CSV. Raw bank exports need mapping; PDF extraction requires an authorized tool outside this skill.

faq.question: Is the workflow fully offline?
faq.answer: The renderer uses bundled assets and local delivery. Agent host retention still applies; explicit version checks contact GitHub, and optional budget integrations use same-origin requests.

faq.question: Can it connect to my bank or move money?
faq.answer: No. It analyzes authorized records and does not collect banking credentials, connect accounts, make payments, or provide investment advice.

faq.question: How are uncertain transactions handled?
faq.answer: The workflow asks for missing facts before affected charts are final. Explicit provisional previews retain visible uncertainty and explain its effect.

faq.question: Which languages and currencies are supported?
faq.answer: The interface supports English and Simplified Chinese. Each report uses one currency with two decimal places; currency conversion is not included.

faq.question: Are reports and budget edits saved automatically?
faq.answer: Reports stay in process memory unless explicitly exported. Budget edits stay in page memory without an integration; card order persists in browser storage.
